turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Hi Linda, how have you been feeling lately?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Hey. Honestly, it's been a tough week. Losing Max still feels so raw.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like Max meant a lot to you.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: He really did. Max was more than just a pet; he was part of the family.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I can imagine it's like a part of your daily life is missing now. How are you coping?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: It helps that David moved in. It's comforting not to be alone in the apartment.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That's good to hear. Having David around must provide some relief. How is the adjustment going?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: It's good, but I feel guilty sometimes. Like I'm burdening him with my grief.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It's understandable to feel that way, but remember, it's okay to lean on someone you trust.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah, he keeps saying he wants to be there for me, but I'm still struggling to accept help.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That can definitely be challenging. What do you think is making it hard to accept his support?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I guess I've always been independent. Relying on someone else feels foreign to me.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That makes sense. Sometimes accepting support is part of growing together. It can be a way to strengthen your bond.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: You're right, and I do appreciate him being here. It's a learning process for both of us.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Absolutely. It's important to give yourself grace during this time.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I appreciate that. Talking about Max and his wagging tail makes me smile, even if it's bittersweet.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Those memories can be quite comforting. Maybe you and David can create a little tribute to Max?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: That's a beautiful idea. I think it might help me honor his memory positively.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I'm glad you think so. Remember, it's okay to grieve and to find comforting ways to remember Max.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thank you for your support. This conversation has really helped me see things from a different perspective.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: You're welcome, Linda. I'm here for you anytime you need to talk.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I appreciate that a lot. I'll talk to David about your suggestion tonight.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Great. I'm sure it'll be a meaningful and healing experience for both of you.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Hi! How are you tonight?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I've been better. I just buried my dog yesterday

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: She was going to turn 15 next month

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Ouch! I'm so sorry to hear that. I never lost a dog, but I've lost cats.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Is 14 a good age for a dog?

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I have my first dog so I don't know much, he is 9 years old and came with our house.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Actually, yes. She was old and had dementia.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: The oldest dog I evet had was 15

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I'm so sorry, losing a pet is very hard on us.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: How did your dog come with the house?

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Was that your only pet? Or do you have others? We moved from FL to KY and the little dog just hung out here, he really belonged to the neighbor's son who didn't want him, so he just ran around wild and wouldn't leave. I never had a dog, but it got cold, so i took him in. They never asked about him and after a week, I asked them if I could have the dog, so they said yes. I don't think they cared.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I wish I could give you a hug, really, there are no words to make this better as you already know the grief of losing a pet, it does get better, but it stings terribly at first.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I have 2 other dogs that are mine and my boyfriend has 2

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thank you. that means a lot

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: We both had dogs when we met.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: So you definitely are a dog lover! I was in my 50s before I ever had a dog, now I wish I had more, they are really loving. Not like cats who don't care much about much except FOOD! lol

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I know when tragedy happens, I can't get stuck in depression, I sort of have to force myself to put one foot in front of the other. It's hard to have a healthy balance between grieving and continuing to live. Cry, then dry my eyes, pick up, go for a walk, don't get caught in grief, but yet don't deny it!

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: They get to be so close and you can really pick up on their emotions and stuff. That's what happens to me. I get stuck sometimes

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I get stuck too. But you are doing the right things, here you reached out to someone and I do care, so you are moving forward.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I always find it helpful just so have someone share my pain with me. Just to know I'm  not alone.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thanks. Another person who has pets helps

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: They understand

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I do understand. My mom died in 2010, right after she died, 1 of my cats died, my husband went into the hospital and almost died, so we went on vacation so I would not be consumed with grief, and do you know, we brought our pets and our cat died when we arrived here on vacation?  I will never forget that. You know what. I knew I could either get consumed in grief, or push through. Man, that was hard. I prayed a lot and God got me through that and I had a good vacation, all things considered.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I will definitely pray for you too that God will comfort your heart and that you will be comforted by your other dogs and your boyfriend's dogs and that you will feel joy at times at the happy memories you had with your dog.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Oh wow, that sounds horrible. Pushing through though I guess is all one can do then. Thank you so much. I believe in prayer.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Prayer is what gets me through every day!  :D  It was rough, but I believe these hard times strengthen us in some way. Because life throws hard balls, and we have to move forward or be consumed.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: That's true. I'm glad I did this project. You really helped me.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I'm so glad I did too. It was a pleasure to meet you. And once again, (hug). :D

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: You too. Thanks so much. bye

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I have one more thing to say - wise words from this 92 year old lady at church named Sue. She told me this after my brother died. When you get older, everyone you know is practically dead.  She said "Life is for the living, if you get caught up to much in all the death, you won't life."  True words. God bless, have a good night.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: HI there, how are you doing?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Hi, I'm ok

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Do you want to talk about whats going on right now?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Sure. I took a nude photo of myself to share with someone I'm dating, and accidentally sent it to several friends in a group chat

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I'm really embarrassed about it and I have some anxiety about meeting or talking to my friends

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Ive done some things like that before. I know this might sound weird but what helped me through it was to actually own it. Take control of it before they can.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Do you think it would be helpful to use humor? I don't want them to tease me about it but I don't know how else to approach it

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Yea that is definitely one way to control it

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Lol maybe some of my friends will share with the group too

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: that would definitely make me feel better about it

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Ha, well that could get interesting

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: yes, for sure

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: anyway, thanks for the chat. this was helpful
